data.narrative:
ADASI, a sovereign-funded Defense & Security company acquired by EDGE Group, was evaluated against a universe of 10 comparables: 2 public-market peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private companies including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems. The target's acquired status and niche positioning within frontier defense tech limit traditional stage-based peer matching.

Peer-median valuation methodology was inapplicable. The Defense & Security sector contains 23 total public and private comparables, but filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier matches yielded fewer than three datapoints in each category—below the minimum threshold of three required for robust median estimation. An all-sector fallback would introduce material bias given the sector's structural differences in capital requirements, regulatory constraints, and exit multiples.

Without sufficient narrow-peer density, this analysis cannot support a triangulated valuation range derived from comparable-company multiples. Instead, the acquisition by EDGE Group—a sovereign-backed entity—suggests the transaction likely reflected strategic defense utility rather than market-rate venture returns. Future valuation work on related frontier-defense assets would benefit from expanded comparable density within the acquired-stage cohort and clearer visibility into exit terms for similar sovereign-backed transactions.
